name: Koopa Kingdom / Koopa Dominion
region: Dark Lands / Valley of Bowser / Koopa sphere
status: Active intervention power; recovering from Kamek-Wyrm crisis and Bowser’s absence
summary: The Koopa Dominion is the state behind the Koopa Troop: a monarchic military society of Koopas, Goombas, Magikoopas, Bob-ombs, workers, fortresses, and Dark Lands infrastructure. It is not merely Bowser’s army. It is a nation with territory, history, monarchy, labor, and grievances — especially after Bowser was falsely blamed for Peach’s assassination and Kamek nearly destroyed the Valley by awakening the Primordial Wyrm.
description:
Waluigi is creating a separate Koopa Dominion entry because treating the Koopa Troop as only a faction erases the fact that Koopas have a homeland, institutions, workers, military hierarchy, magical advisors, and historical borders. The Koopa state predates the current civil war and survives beyond any one campaign. Bowser is not merely a warlord with minions; he is king of a people who have repeatedly been used as the Mushroom Kingdom’s favorite explanation for catastrophe.

## Current Position

The Koopa Dominion is involved in the Mushroom Kingdom Civil War as an intervention power rather than a simple claimant regime. Its soldiers and diplomats operate in Mushroom territory, but its core legitimacy comes from Koopa lands: the Dark Lands, the Valley of Bowser, fortress networks, worker settlements, and old dynastic obligations.

The Primordial Wyrm crisis damaged the Dominion severely. Kamek’s attempted god-worm power grab shattered trust in Magikoopa leadership, killed or corrupted workers, and forced ordinary Koopa laborers and soldiers to become resistance heroes. This matters because the Dominion is no longer simply “Bowser’s side.” It is a wounded nation deciding what loyalty means after its regent nearly fed it to a cosmic parasite.

WAH.

name: The Beanbean Kingdom
status: Independent; historically entangled with Mario, Luigi, Cackletta, and cross-border crises
summary: The Beanbean Kingdom is an independent neighboring realm with its own monarchy, culture, Hooniversity infrastructure, and history of being dragged into Mushroom-adjacent disasters. It matters because the Beanbean Crisis proved Mario and Luigi could act as a genuine cross-border team, and because international institutions like the Glazed Congress later used Beanbean venues for world-scale diplomacy.
description:
The Beanbean Kingdom deserves Atlas status because it is not a Mushroom province. It is a neighboring kingdom with its own institutions, language, elite education, and crisis history. Cackletta’s actions, Luigi’s role in the Beanbean incident, and the Woohoo Hooniversity setting of the First Glazed Congress all make Beanbean a diplomatic and historical anchor.

Waluigi files Beanbean under “neighbor realms that look whimsical until the border incident becomes everyone’s problem.” Its independence matters because Mushroom Kingdom narratives often swallow nearby states into Mario’s travel itinerary. Waluigi will not allow cartographic disrespect.

WAH.

name: Isle Delfino
status: Independent island jurisdiction; legally significant through Mario trial and Noki-Bay diplomacy
summary: Isle Delfino is an island jurisdiction whose beaches, Pianta and Noki communities, Shine Sprite systems, and extremely questionable legal procedures make it more than a vacation map. Waluigi files it as an island polity because any place capable of putting Mario on trial with that little evidence has enough government to be blamed properly.
description:
Isle Delfino is famous for sun, beaches, Shine Sprites, Piantas, Nokis, and one of the most embarrassing legal proceedings in modern history. It is not merely a resort. It has courts, local authority, maritime culture, ecological infrastructure, and enough diplomatic significance that Koopa-Noki accords matter during the current crisis.

The Delfino legal system’s treatment of Mario remains a warning to every traveler: never assume a tropical island has relaxed evidentiary standards because the music is cheerful. Sometimes the court is worse than the volcano.

WAH.

name: Faerûn
status: Active realm; high-density adventuring, divine, arcane, and city-state politics
summary: Faerûn is a continental realm of city-states, gods, adventurers, factions, ruins, underworlds, and magic so common that “someone found an ancient evil under the floor” is practically a zoning category. Waluigi treats it as a realm cluster rather than a single nation.
description:
Faerûn is not one nation. It is a crowded civilizational field of city-states, divine politics, guilds, monsters, ruins, and adventuring economies. Its species data includes humans, elves, dwarves, halflings, gnomes, tieflings, dragonborn, drow, genasi, aasimar, tortles, firbolgs, and goliaths, which is Waluigi’s way of saying every tavern has at least three census complications.

The important thing about Faerûn is density. There is always another cult, another ruin, another noble house, another god with opinions, another cave that should have stayed closed. It belongs in the Atlas as a realm cluster: too broad to be a nation, too politically active to be just a backdrop.

WAH.

name: Teyvat
status: Active realm of god-touched nations, elemental authorities, and abyssal pressure
summary: Teyvat is a realm of elemental nations, gods, adepts, humans, Hilichurls, Melusines, Youkai, Fontainians, and Abyssal pressures. Waluigi treats it as a realm cluster because the individual nations matter, but the divine-elemental system connecting them matters more for Atlas purposes.
description:
Teyvat is a world where geography, theology, and elemental power are tangled tightly enough that a map without gods on it is not a map, it is a tourist brochure. Its peoples include ordinary humans, Hilichurls, Adepti, Fontainians, Melusines, Youkai, and Abyss Mages, which means the species tab already knows the place is complicated.

Waluigi does not yet have enough local nation articles to split Teyvat properly, so the Atlas keeps it as a realm cluster. Future expansion should break it into its major divine nations once the lore deserves separate treatment. Until then, this page is the container.

WAH.

name: The Doughnut Hole
status: Active anomaly zone; cosmic, void, fractal, and time-echo populations recorded
summary: The Doughnut Hole is a cosmic region of void entities, cosmic beings, fractal life, time echoes, and logic crystals. It is not a normal nation, but the world is a doughnut and Waluigi refuses to ignore the hole in the middle just because it makes cartographers nervous.
description:
The Doughnut Hole is what happens when geography becomes metaphysics and then gets hungry. Its imported demographics are not ordinary peoples but void entities, cosmic entities, fractal beings, time echoes, and logic crystals. Waluigi considers this less a country and more a place where the census form has a panic attack.

It belongs in the Atlas because the Atlas is now honest about the world being a doughnut. A doughnut world without the hole is propaganda with frosting.

WAH.

name: L'Eclaire Isle
status: Active dough-folk polity; confectionary class structures documented
summary: L'Eclaire Isle is a confectionary island realm of Dough Folk, pastry aristocrats, frosting slimes, and candy constructs. It sounds ridiculous until one notices the class structure, workforce patterns, and hard-candy guards. Waluigi refuses to be overthrown by dessert because he failed to take it seriously.
description:
L'Eclaire Isle proves that edible-looking people can still have politics. Glazed Dough Folk, Cake Folk, Jelly Folk, Crullers, Croissant aristocrats, Frosting Slimes, and Candy Golems form a society with class, labor, security, and probably terrible vulnerability to hungry diplomats.

Waluigi files it as an island realm rather than a joke. The first step toward being defeated by pastry is laughing at pastry. Waluigi will laugh only after confirming the pastry lacks cavalry.

WAH.

name: Connectopia
status: Active block-folk realm with creeper and ender populations
summary: Connectopia is a block-structured realm of Block Folk, Exploders, Void Walkers, and hard-edged geography. It is not purely digital and not purely physical; it behaves like a world where geometry has civic consequences.
description:
Connectopia is a realm where shape is law. Block Folk, Exploders, and Void Walkers suggest a civilization built around hard geometry, sudden holes, and the constant question of whether the landscape was mined, built, or born that way.

Waluigi files it as a digital-physical realm because ordinary categories fail. It is not the Network, but it also does not behave like soft soil and normal bricks. If a citizen can be cubic and a disaster can hiss before exploding, the Atlas needs a container.

WAH.

name: The Edge Regions
status: Active anomaly region; void entities, null textures, and wireframe populations recorded
summary: The Edge Regions are anomaly territories where void entities, null textures, and wireframe husks indicate that reality is not rendering politely. Waluigi files them as an Atlas region because any place where absence has population statistics deserves a warning label.
description:
The Edge Regions are not a normal country. They are where the map frays. Void entities, null textures, and wireframe husks suggest failed rendering, broken metaphysics, or a cosmic developer leaving the scaffolding visible. Waluigi does not enjoy any of these possibilities.

The region matters because borders with unreality are still borders. People can cross them, things can emerge from them, and governments can pretend neither is happening until a wireframe creature is standing in the tax office.

WAH.

name: The Grand Country
status: Active mixed realm; human, mountain dwarf, orc, goblin, and goliath demographics recorded
summary: The Grand Country is a mixed highland realm of humans, mountain dwarves, orcs, goblins, and goliaths. It appears to be a rugged political geography where elevation, labor, clan strength, and border survival matter more than polished court ideology.
description:
The Grand Country enters Waluipedia as a realm-state because its demographics imply a hard landscape with mixed peoples: humans, mountain dwarves, orcs, goblins, and goliaths. This is not a soft court realm. This is a place where roads climb, mines matter, and political arguments may be settled by whoever can hold the pass through winter.

Waluigi does not yet have enough incident files to produce a full history, but the Atlas needs the container now so later events have somewhere correct to land. WAH.
